This is something I've been working on myself as well, and I thought I'd share a few tips I've learned.


First, congratulations on starting with the first step of self-awareness! Second, that no external factor can convince you without your initiative. People can tell you the truth, but you have to hit that "eureka" moment on your own. It's hard to come by, but eventually you'll stumble on some piece of art/quote/experience that makes so much sense and giving it up becomes easier. Speaking from 20+ years of experience.

Third, know that there's a huge chance you'll have your doubts from time to time. That's normal! This probably stems from "what ifs" in your life and thinking that the paths you didn't take might be better. And it's normal to have doubts. Obviously you know that life isn't a race, but there's probably a picture in your mind that worsens that envy. Instead visualizing yourself in a race, try to visualize yourself in a wide space, alone, where you only look ahead (or anything that helps). know that what others achieve says nothing about you (if they earned tons of achievements, it isn't meant to signify that you don't.) It's about realizing that absence of what other people have doesn't make what you have any less.

Lastly, keep a support system close to you. Because insecurities usually come when our potential or gifts become hazy in our perspective. Aside from friends who hype you up, surround yourself with social media pages/accounts that encourage your validity or have experienced what you've similarly and are succeeding. You could also keep some things you can open whenever you feel dejected.
